inputs.share_count_basis: 264,778,000 shares in issue excluding 1,888,800 treasury shares at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim report, corporate governance section). No options, RSUs or awards outstanding: the 2025 Share Incentive Scheme has had no awards granted (interim report, scheme disclosure). Held FLAT; SBC is zero so there is nothing to expense or dilute. H1 FY2026 buyback of US$3.9m (treasury shares) is the only share-count movement since listing.
inputs.cash_note: Cash and cash equivalents US$111.577m plus bank deposits with original maturity over three months US$51.018m, both at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim, condensed statement of financial position). No interest-bearing bank or other borrowings at 30 June 2026 (interim, gearing-ratio note). total_debt is lease liabilities only (US$1.522m), lease treatment (A).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report note on profit before tax and H1 FY2026 interim: no share-based payment expense in any period FY2023-H1 FY2026; 2025 Share Incentive Scheme adopted pre-listing with no awards granted or outstanding. Equity-award taxes 0.
inputs.buyback_note: US$3.876m of shares repurchased into treasury in H1 FY2026 (financing activities). FY2023-FY2025: nil. The flat count is funded, not a convention; but the count is flat anyway because SBC is zero.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows in USD (filing headers 'US$'000'; FY2025 AR and H1 FY2026 interim). HKEX quote in HKD. Per-share values computed in USD and converted at USD/HKD 7.8423 (Yahoo Finance HKD=X, 2026-10-23). Parity check: no dual listing; the HKD is pegged in a 7.75-7.85 band, so the rate cannot be more than 0.6% off in either direction. Cross-check of direction: IPO offer HK$27.80 x 41,666,800 new shares = HK$1,158m gross, which the FY2025 AR states as US$138m net at 7.8475 -- consistent with HKD = USD x 7.8x, not the inverse.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are USD, so WACC is built from USD inputs. Rebuilt 2026-10-24 after the multiples sanity check tripped (diagnosis: wacc_too_low; structural risks not priced by a standard WACC). CAPM base: 10-year UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta 1.0 (a consumer-staple beta; the prior build's beta 1.2 carried the concentration risk implicitly, and is reset to 1.0 so the explicit premiums below are not stacked on top of it) = 9.2%. Explicit premiums per the Step 8c.5 template: (1) Small-cap illiquidity +2.0% -- market cap ~US$143m at HK$4.23 (template band 1.5-2.5% for < US$300m), controlling Thai shareholder holds the majority of the register, and removal from Stock Connect in September 2026 took Mainland buyers out of the pool, so a discount to cash can persist for years. (2) Single-customer concentration +1.5% -- FY2025 AR 'Major customers and suppliers': the largest customer (a distributor) was 50.9% of total sales and the top five 97.2%; above the template's >40% threshold. Charged at the low end of 1.5-2.5% because the distributor is a channel to many retailers rather than an end customer, and the company is building direct channel relationships and a licensed China import entity (H1 FY2026 interim). (3) Concentrated geographic / regulatory risk +1.5% -- ~90% of FY2025 revenue into Mainland China as an imported Thai product. The template's geographic band is 0.5-1.5% and the regulatory single-point-of-failure band 1.0-2.0%; here they are the SAME risk (Chinese import, food-safety and labelling regulation on one product category into one market), so one premium at the top of the geographic band is charged rather than two overlapping ones -- charging both would double-count. Total: 9.2 + 2.0 + 1.5 + 1.5 = 14.2%. No debt, so WACC = cost of equity. Applied to all three scenarios -- operating risk (supply, channel rebuild, China demand) stays in the scenario flows and the 35% bear weight, not in per-scenario discount rates (charge risk once). Not charged: extreme cyclicality (coconut water is a staple; the 2026 collapse is a supply shock and share loss, both already in the flows). Prior WACC 11.0% (10.2% CAPM at beta 1.2 + 0.8% illiquidity).
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. IFRS 16 lease liabilities of US$1.522m at 30 June 2026 sit in total_debt; lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows and no lease_cost_pct_path is charged. Right-of-use depreciation (US$0.12m/yr) stays inside D&A. Immaterial either way: total lease cash is ~0.1% of revenue.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. IFB Thailand is 99.89% owned (interim, dividend-rights note); NCI is nil in the consolidated statements. Flows are treated as 100% attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing: non-US operating consumer company; adaptations file read for currency bridge, leases, SBC-zero and interest-income/matching-asset rule). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. OWNER FCF: reported FCF FY2025 11.867 less SBC 0 less interest income 3.381 = 8.486. Interest income is stripped because net cash (US$161m) is ~19x the FCF base and is added back in the bridge at face value -- leaving the ~US$5.7m annualised interest in the flows would count the pile twice. SBC-ZERO: house and street coincide; band_position is null. BUSINESS: asset-light coconut-water brand owner ('if', 'Innococo'); production outsourced to the Thai controlling shareholder's OEM (purchases of inventories from the holding company are a related-party line), ~90% of FY2025 revenue into Mainland China through distributors. IPO 30 June 2025 at HK$27.80; price is now 85% below that. H1 FY2026 revenue fell 46.7% on a PET/packaging/coconut-water supply shortage from April 2026, the self-inflicted Innococo channel restructuring (brand revenue 26.2 in FY2024 to 1.7 in H1 FY2026), and softer category demand; EBITDA margin collapsed to 5.5% with marketing at 12.1% of revenue. No numeric FY2026 guidance exists; management says product availability has been 'progressively restored'. FY0 = FY2025 (last audited year); year 1 = FY2026 and its growth rate is set off the actual H1 (US$50.4m) plus a judged H2. CAPEX: historically negligible (0.1-0.3% of revenue) because manufacturing is outsourced; H1 FY2026 stepped up to US$1.4m (localised China production, Shanghai cafe), held at 1-1.5% of revenue. WORKING CAPITAL: distributor model, trade receivables 19.2 at Dec 2025 (11% of revenue) vs payables to the OEM 16.2; net WC is a few percent of revenue, so growth consumes cash at wc_capture -5% of the revenue change (negative capture; in a revenue-decline year it releases cash, which is exactly what H1 FY2026 showed: receivables 19.2 to 5.4). PRICE vs CASH: at HK$4.23 the equity is worth US$143m against US$161m of net cash, i.e. the market assigns the operating business a negative value. The scenarios do not discount the cash; the bear case instead lets the business consume some of it through two loss-making years, and the bear weight is raised to 35%.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case FY2026-trough to FY2031 revenue CAGR (recovery path), not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Only three fiscal years exist (FY2023-FY2025, company incorporated Feb 2024 as the listing vehicle), so 3- and 5-year CAGRs cannot be computed. The 2-year revenue CAGR of 42% (87.4 to 176.4) is pre-collapse and is not a forward input: H1 FY2026 revenue was -46.7% YoY. Equity CAGR is meaningless (9.5 to 170.8 is the US$138m IPO, not retained earnings). Owner FCF fell from 40.5 (FY2024) to 8.5 (FY2025) on a receivables build and heavier marketing, a -79% change while revenue grew 12% -- reported growth was not converting to cash before the supply shock hit.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less interest income): FY2024 41.566 - 0 - 1.096 = 40.470; FY2025 11.867 - 0 - 3.381 = 8.486; H1 FY2026 9.555 - 0 - 2.870 = 6.685. FY2023 FCF not disclosed in the CSV.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 = H1 actual 50.4 + H2 ~59 as supply is restored = ~109 (-38%). Then a recovery that regains the FY2025 revenue level only by FY2031 (category growing ~13% p.a. per the interim's industry data; the brand regains distributor shelf space but not its pre-shock share), fading to 3% by year 10.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 EBITDA margin 5% (H1 5.5%, marketing 12% of revenue). Rebuilds to a mature 17%: between the FY2025 normalised ~18.5% (ex 4.1 listing fees, 1.3 inventory write-down, 1.8 FX loss) and a world where marketing stays at 8-10% of revenue rather than the 4.7% of FY2024's 25.6% peak. Gross margin assumed to recover from 28.9% to ~33%, not to FY2024's 36.7%.
base.tax_rationale: Thailand 20%, Singapore 17%, HK 16.5%, Mainland 25%; FY2025 ETR 20.2% on operating profit. Interest income is tax-exempt in Singapore but is stripped from the flows anyway. 20% flat on EBIT; the engine credits no tax on a loss.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 2.5% vs a 15x cap: a lower cap than the 20x house default because this is a single-category, single-market brand with a related-party supply chain.

bull.growth_rationale: Supply fully normalises in H2 FY2026 (FY2026 ~115, -35%), the rebuilt direct China sales organisation and local manufacturing restore 'if' to its FY2025 run-rate during FY2027, and international (Taiwan, USA, Philippines, Australia all growing strongly off small bases) plus the Roasted Coconut Water line add a second leg. Revenue passes FY2025's level in FY2028 and reaches ~2x by year 10.
bull.margin_rationale: Mature 22%: marketing intensity normalises toward 7-8% as the Innococo relaunch spend rolls off, gross margin recovers to ~35% with local China production, operating leverage on a fixed cost base of ~US$15m. Still below FY2024's 25.6% peak.

bear.growth_rationale: H2 FY2026 no better than H1 (FY2026 ~97, -45%), then a further 10% decline in FY2027 as Chinese distributors that were starved of product in 2026 do not come back, local competitors (Vita Coco China, domestic brands) fill the shelf, and Innococo never rebuilds. Revenue stabilises around US$87m -- the FY2023 level -- and grows with inflation.
bear.margin_rationale: Sub-scale brand carrying a listed-company cost base and continued marketing spend to defend share: EBITDA margin 1% in FY2026, -2% in FY2027 (a cash-burning year), then a slow climb to 8% as spend is cut. The business is worth little more than its cash; the two loss-making years and the 12x cap are how the scenario consumes part of the pile rather than discounting the cash directly.

scenario_narratives.base: Supply-shock-then-recovery. The April 2026 PET/packaging/coconut-water shortage is what management says it is -- transitory -- and product availability is restored through H2 FY2026, but the half-year of empty distributor shelves in Mainland China, the Innococo channel teardown and softer category sentiment mean 'if' regains its FY2025 revenue only around FY2031. Marketing stays structurally higher than the 4.7% of revenue that produced FY2024's 25.6% EBITDA margin, so the mature margin settles at 17%. Owner FCF roughly tracks NOPAT because the business is asset-light; the US$161m cash pile is the floor under the value and is added at face.
scenario_narratives.bull: The dedicated China sales organisation, licensed import/export entity and local manufacturing that were built during H1 FY2026 convert into headquarters-to-headquarters relationships with key channel accounts, shortening the route to market and taking out a distributor margin layer. Supply normalises fully, the Roasted Coconut Water line (sales +100% YoY) and international markets (Taiwan +31%, USA +133%, Philippines, Laos, Australia IGA) add a second leg, and revenue is back above FY2025 by FY2028 on a 22% mature margin. The IPO narrative, a year late.
scenario_narratives.bear: The supply shortage was the visible cause but not the only one: H2 FY2025 revenue was already down 5% YoY before the shock, Innococo had collapsed 63% in FY2025, and the 85% share-price fall since the IPO encodes a loss of distributor and investor confidence that the filings do not spell out. Press reports cited in the Analysis JSON put 'if''s offline China coconut-water share at ~30% by Q3 2025 against a 60%+ peak, so share was being lost before any supply shock. Chinese distributors re-source to domestic and Vita Coco brands, 'if' settles back to FY2023 scale (~US$87m), the listed cost base and defensive marketing produce two loss-making years, and the company ends up a cash box with a small, low-margin brand attached. Governance axes in this scenario: production is bought from the controlling shareholder's OEM (related-party purchases), and US$42m of pre-IPO dividends were paid out in H1 2025 -- the cash is real but the minority's claim on it depends on the board. Removal from Stock Connect in September 2026 removes Mainland buyers from the register, which does not change the cash flows but does mean the discount to cash can persist for a long time.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 35%: the recovery thesis rests on management's unverified supply-shortage explanation, revenue was already softening before the shock, ~90% of revenue is one market sold through distributors who were starved of product for a half-year, the OEM is a related party, and a newly listed stock down 85% in sixteen months is the market saying it does not believe the cash-plus-brand arithmetic. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right at once (supply, China channel rebuild, international scale-up). Base 45%. Analysis JSON corroborates: China share reportedly halved from its peak before the shock, FY2025 net profit already fell 32%, and Stock Connect removal (Sept 2026) shrinks the buyer pool.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Asset-light brand owner valued on owner FCF with interest income stripped and the US$161m net cash added once in the bridge. The valuation is dominated by the cash: at HK$4.23 the market capitalisation is below net cash, so the operating business is being priced at less than zero. The scenarios ask whether the brand is worth anything after the 2026 supply shock, not whether the 2024 hypergrowth repeats -- the base case does not regain FY2025 revenue until FY2031 and the mature margin is held well below the FY2024 peak. The hurdle entry price and required-return table are reported in HKD alongside the USD computation.
key_risks_to_valuation: The net cash is ~113% of the market cap; any leakage of that cash (related-party transactions with the controlling shareholder's OEM, special dividends to the pre-IPO holders, acquisitions announced in the outlook) changes the value one-for-one and is not in any scenario.
Supply-shock narrative unverified: if H2 FY2026 revenue does not improve on H1's US$50.4m, the base case's -38% FY2026 is too optimistic and the bear's -45% is the base.
Mainland China concentration (~90% of FY2025 revenue) through distributors; distributor destocking and share loss to domestic brands is a one-way door for a premium imported brand.
Marketing intensity: 12% of revenue in H1 FY2026 vs 4.7% in FY2024. The mature 17% EBITDA margin assumes it settles at 8-10%; every 1pp of marketing is ~1pp of margin.
Thai Baht appreciation squeezes gross margin (USD-priced sales, THB-costed procurement) -- FY2025 GP margin fell 3.8pp partly on this.
Only three years of history; no cycle has been observed. The 42% 2-year revenue CAGR is not a forward input.
valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_response: The multiples sanity check tripped on 'base upside 159% with price in the upper half of the 10-year range'. The second half of that trigger is an artifact: only 17 monthly closes exist (IPO 30 June 2025), the stock has only ever fallen (HK$36.60 to HK$4.23, price is at the BOTTOM of its range), and the one historical multiple row (FY2025: P/B 192x, EV/EBITDA 1226x) is a single IPO-peak data point on a tiny pre-collapse equity base, further inflated by the known fx-direction handling in the historical table. So the 'historical average' is not a market-set ceiling. The diagnosis (WACC too low for structural risk) is nonetheless taken at face: WACC raised from 11.0% to 14.2% with explicit illiquidity, single-distributor and China concentration premiums (see inputs.wacc_rationale). The upside that remains is the cash: net cash of US$161m is US$0.61 (HK$4.77) per share against a HK$4.23 price, so even a zero-value operating business implies ~13% upside before any discount rate is applied. The discount rate only touches the operating-business slice of the value, which is the smaller part in every scenario.
